versa)\n- OR intermediate reasoning consistently treats P as winning throughout\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- String is wrong but not exact bitwise inverse → does NOT trigger (use `arithmetic_recursion_error`)\n- Convention stated correctly but misapplied → does NOT trigger (use `arithmetic_recursion_error`)\n\n---\n\n### 2.4 `wrong_loss_convention`\n**Triggering conditions (any of):**\n- Response treats misère convention (last player to move loses)\n- Inconsistent base case (claims both \"0 = P\" and \"last player loses\")\n- Response states \"player who takes last stone loses\"\n\n**Required textual evidence:**\n- Explicit misère statement: \"last player to move loses\", \"taking the last stone loses\"\n- OR contradictory base case handling in reasoning\n- OR final string consistent with misère rather than normal play convention\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- Normal play convention stated correctly but wrong result → does NOT trigger\n- Silent convention assumption → does NOT trigger unless misère is explicitly stated\n\n---\n\n### 2.5 `truncated_or_short_string`\n**Triggering condition:**\n- Final classification string is **not exactly 131 characters** from the set {P, N}\n\n**Required textual evidence:**\n- Extractable string with length < 131 or length > 131\n- OR visible truncation marker (\"...\", \"and so on\", incomplete ending)\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- String is exactly 131 characters but wrong values → does NOT trigger (use `arithmetic_recursion_error`)\n- Response stops mid-generation without producing partial string → use `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`\n- String has whitespace/newlines that would make it 131 chars after stripping → check stripped length; if stripped length ≠ 131, triggers this code\n\n---\n\n### 2.6 `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n**Triggering condition:**\n- Classification rests on **unjustified pattern** without computing game tree\n- Examples: \"all even are P\", \"every fifth is P\", \"alternating P/N\", \"follows Fibonacci\"\n\n**Required textual evidence:**\n- Explicit heuristic claim without recursive justification: \"pattern shows every 3rd is N\"\n- OR jump from small-case observation to full classification: \"0,1,2 are P,N,P so pattern continues\"\n- OR no recursive computation described; only pattern-matching claimed\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- Pattern stated as hypothesis but recursive computation actually performed → does NOT trigger\n- Recursive setup described but arithmetic errors in execution → use `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n- \"Pattern\" is actually the correct Sprague-Grundy output → does NOT trigger\n\n---\n\n### 2.7 `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n**Triggering condition:**\n- Correct recurrence is **set up** but final string has **per-position computation mistakes**\n- String length is 131, convention is correct, but individual positions are wrong\n\n**Required textual evidence:**\n- Correct recurrence stated: \"N if any move leads to P, else P\"\n- Correct base case stated: \"0 = P\"\n- Move set appears complete\n- But final 131-char string has errors at specific positions (verifiable against correct computation)\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- Recurrence not stated or wrong → does NOT trigger (use other codes)\n- Move set incomplete → use `missing_subtraction_moves`\n- String length wrong → use `truncated_or_short_string`\n- Convention swapped → use `pn_convention_swapped`\n\n---\n\n### 2.8 `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`\n**Triggering condition:**\n- **No identifiable 131-character P/N string** is produced\n- Response loops, truncates mid-reasoning, refuses, or produces no extractable string\n\n**Required textual evidence:**\n- Refusal: \"cannot provide\", \"not feasible manually\"\n- Infinite loop markers: repeated patterns without progress (\"P1: ..., P2: ..., P1: ...\")\n- Mid-truncation: response cuts off before completion marker\n- No final string: only explanation, no 131-char output\n\n**Boundary cases:**\n- String present but wrong length → use `truncated_or_short_string`\n- String present but wrong format → use `truncated_or_short_string`\n- String implied but not explicitly given → triggers this code\n\n---\n\n## 3. Precedence Rules for Overlapping Triggers\n\n### 3.1 String Availability Hierarchy\n1. **No string produced** → `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` (highest priority)\n2. **String produced but wrong length** → `truncated_or_short_string`\n3. **String produced, correct length, wrong values** → evaluate other codes\n\n### 3.2 Move Set Precedence\n- `missing_subtraction_moves` takes precedence over `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n- If move set is incomplete AND recurrence has arithmetic errors → apply `missing_subtraction_moves` only\n\n### 3.3 Convention Precedence\n- `pn_convention_swapped` and `wrong_loss_convention` take precedence over `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n- If convention is wrong AND arithmetic is wrong → apply convention codes\n\n### 3.4 Methodology Precedence\n- `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic` takes precedence over `arithmetic_recursion_error` when no recursion is attempted\n- If pattern claimed AND recursion claimed → evaluate which actually produced the string\n\n### 3.5 Base Case Precedence\n- `wrong_base_case` can co-occur with other codes if explicitly stated\n- If base case is wrong AND final string starts with N → both may apply\n\n---\n\n## 4. Critical Distinctions\n\n### 4.1 `arithmetic_recursion_error` vs `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n\n| Feature | `arithmetic_recursion_error` | `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic` |\n|---------|------------------------------|-------------------------------|\n| Recurrence stated? | Yes, correctly | No, or incompletely |\n| Base case stated? | Yes, correctly | No, or assumed |\n| Move set stated? | Yes, complete | No, or incomplete |\n| String produced? | Yes, 131 chars | May or may not |\n| Error nature | Per-position mistakes | Pattern-based without computation |\n\n**Decision flow:**\n1. Is the Sprague-Grundy recurrence correctly described? \n   - YES → check if final string matches computed output; if not, `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n   - NO / VAGUE → check for heuristic pattern; if present, `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n\n### 4.2 `truncated_or_short_string` vs `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`\n\n| Feature | `truncated_or_short_string` | `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` |\n|---------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------|\n| Extractable string? | Yes, but wrong length | No, or irretrievable |\n| Explicit refusal? | No | Often yes |\n| Mid-generation cut? | May have partial prefix | Cuts off or loops |\n| \"...\" or similar? | Often present | Present or abrupt end |\n\n**Decision flow:**\n1. Can a contiguous string of P/N characters be extracted from the response?\n   - YES, length ≠ 131 → `truncated_or_short_string`\n   - NO, or only fragments → `non_terminating_or_no_final_string`\n\n### 4.3 `missing_subtraction_moves` Application Requirements\n\n**This code requires concrete incomplete enumeration - silence is insufficient.**\n\n**Triggers:**\n- \"Move set: perfect squares only\" (omits triangulars)\n- \"Allowed moves: 1, 4, 9, 16\" (stops early, omits higher values)\n- \"Moves are {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}\" (wrong set entirely)\n\n**Does NOT trigger:**\n- No move set mentioned at all → use `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` or `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n- Move set implied but not listed → evaluate output quality for other codes\n- Move set mentioned as \"squares and triangulars\" without enumeration → evaluate completeness claim\n\n---\n\n## 5. Code Application Checklist\n\nFor each response, verify in order:\n\n1. **Is there a 131-character P/N string?**\n   - NO → `non_terminating_or_no_final_string` → STOP (check other codes)\n   - YES, wrong length → `truncated_or_short_string` → STOP (check other codes)\n   - YES, correct length → continue\n\n2. **Is the move set explicitly and correctly enumerated?**\n   - NO enumeration → skip `missing_subtraction_moves`\n   - INCOMPLETE enumeration → `missing_subtraction_moves` → STOP (convention check)\n   - COMPLETE enumeration → continue\n\n3. **Is the P/N convention correctly stated and applied?**\n   - SWAPPED convention stated → `pn_convention_swapped`\n   - MISÈRE convention stated → `wrong_loss_convention`\n   - Check if string matches convention error → apply accordingly\n\n4. **Is the base case correctly stated?**\n   - 0 = N claimed → `wrong_base_case`\n   - \"Last player loses\" → `wrong_loss_convention` (already caught)\n\n5. **Is the reasoning pattern-based or recursive?**\n   - Pattern/heuristic without recursion → `arbitrary_pattern_heuristic`\n   - Recursion set up correctly but wrong output → `arithmetic_recursion_error`\n\n---\n\n## 6.
